description:
## Why this issue exists

Stoa can be started with debug/dev-mode flags (e.g., `--dev`, env vars, config keys like `auth.bypass = true`) that disable authentication or weaken security controls. If such a flag is accidentally set in a production deployment, security is silently bypassed.

SOC2 CC6.1 requires that production environments enforce access controls. An auditor will ask how we prevent dev flags from reaching production.

## What needs to be done

- Audit all config keys and env vars that disable or weaken security (auth bypass, TLS skip-verify, plaintext fallback, debug endpoints).
- At startup, if any such key is set AND the environment is not explicitly `dev` or `test`, abort with a fatal error and a clear log message.
- The environment classification must itself be explicit: default to `production` mode; require an explicit `ENV=development` or equivalent to permit dev flags.
- Add a startup banner that logs the active environment classification.

## Acceptance criteria

- Starting with `auth.bypass=true` in production mode fails with a fatal error at startup
- Starting with the same flag in development mode succeeds with a loud warning
- CI test suite runs in `test` mode and passes
- Environment classification appears in startup log

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: SOC2 CC6.1.

title: Dev mode startup guard
